{{recipesummary | Category = Indian recipes | Time = soak: 8 hours
prep: 20-50 minutes | Difficulty = 3 | Rating = 2 }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]] '''Cheyeeam''' are deep-fried balls of ground chickpeas. ==Ingredients== * ½ [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] [[Cookbook:Chickpea|''kadalai paruppu'']] (Bengal gram, small brown chickpeas) * ½ kg [[Cookbook:Jaggery|''vellam'']] (jaggery, unrefined palm sugar) * 10 [[Cookbook:Cardamom|''elackai'']] (cardamom pods) * ½ kg [[Cookbook:Maida|''maida mavu'']] (refined wheat flour) * [[Cookbook:Water|Water]] * [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste * 1 [[Cookbook:Liter|litre]] [[cookbook:Oil|cooking oil]] ==Procedure== # Soak ''kadalai paruppu'' in clean water for at least 8 hours. They will double in size, so allow extra water for them to soak up. # [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] ''kadalai paruppu''. This should take about 40 minutes in a regular pot on the stove, or about 9 minutes in a [[Cookbook:Pressure Cooking|pressure cooker]] (plus 10 minutes to depressurise). # Grind boiled ''kadalai paruppu'' with the jaggery and ''elachi'', without adding any water, to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. # Make small balls with the dough. # Make a thin [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]] with the ''maida'' and water. Add salt as needed. # Dip the dough balls in the batter. # Pour the oil in a pan. Heat until a small piece of dough floats and bubbles when added. # Add a few battered dough balls. [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|Deep fry]] individually until golden. [[Category:Indian recipes]] [[Category:Vegan recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using chickpea]] [[Category:Recipes with metric units]] [[Category:Recipes using cardamom]] [[Category:Recipes using wheat flour]] [[Category:Recipes using jaggery]]
